Chapter 4: Emotion—Why Feelings Drive People to Share and Spread Ideas
Let’s dive into something that really shapes the way ideas move—emotion.
Beyond wanting to look good or just following cues from the world around us, it’s our feelings that truly push us to share. Think about it: when something sparks a strong reaction—joy, awe, anger, or even anxiety—you’re just more likely to pass it on, right? That surge of emotion acts like fuel, giving people the energy to talk, post, or forward what they’ve seen.
But here’s the thing—not all emotions have the same effect. High-energy feelings like excitement, amusement, surprise, or outrage? They’re especially powerful. They create this sense of urgency, almost daring you to get others involved. On the other hand, emotions like contentment or sadness, which are lower in intensity, can actually dampen the urge to share. They make us feel more settled, less likely to spread the word.
Picture this: you watch a heartwarming video of a rescue animal. That rush of joy and compassion makes you want to send it to everyone you know. Or maybe you come across a news story that sparks outrage. It’s almost impossible not to share it, right? You want others to feel what you’re feeling, to join in, or maybe even take action.
Emotions are like social glue. When you share something that made you laugh or left you speechless, you’re inviting your friends to feel the same way. It’s about connection and belonging—bringing people together through shared experience.
You can really see this in the way certain stories or campaigns just take off. A charity appeal that tugs at your heart is way more likely to go viral than a simple list of statistics. And when a product demo genuinely amazes or delights, people can’t help but talk about it.
So, how do you harness this power of emotion? It’s all about creating messages and experiences that truly move people. Not by manipulating or exaggerating, but by tapping into feelings that are real and relatable. You want your content to be something people just can’t help but share—because it made them feel something.
Here are a few practical ways to make that happen:
- Craft stories or messages that spark awe, excitement, or amusement. - Highlight the unexpected—surprising details or twists that get a strong reaction. - Focus on topics or issues that naturally bring out high-energy emotions.
And remember, it’s not just about making people happy. Positive emotions like joy or inspiration are great, but even negative high-arousal feelings—like anger or anxiety—can motivate people to share. The real driver is how strongly someone feels, not just whether the feeling is good or bad.
Emotion works alongside things like social currency and triggers. When people feel something deeply, they’re way more likely to spread the word—especially if sharing lifts their social standing or connects to something that’s top of mind.
So, if you want your ideas or products to really catch on, make sure you’re tapping into those emotional drivers. Because when you move people, you motivate them to share—and that’s when things truly go viral.
